quizzes.stem: A team reviews a fourteen-file change by sending all the files in one request. The comments are deep for the first files and thin for the last ones, and a changed signature in one file is never matched against its callers elsewhere. Which restructuring fits best?

options.a: Give each source its own examination, then run a pass over what they concluded
options.b: Send the same single request three times and merge the answers into one report
options.c: Split the change into two halves of seven files and review each half in one request
options.d: Keep the single request and add an instruction to treat every file with equal care

explanation.a: Each file gets a full review in its own context, and a second pass sees the relations.
explanation.b: Ruled out because repetition keeps what causes the problem: "A request that holds a dozen files spends that budget on text before the review begins".
explanation.c: Ruled out because halves keep the dilution and still hide the relations between the halves: "The exam calls the effect attention dilution".
explanation.d: Ruled out because an instruction does not change what fills the context: "LLM performance degrades as context fills".

quizzes.stem: A team must add tests to a large legacy codebase that it does not know. Which order of work does the exam expect?

options.a: Fix one subtask per directory in advance and run them in order
options.b: Ask the model to plan every test in advance, then run that plan to the end
options.c: Map the structure, rank the areas by impact, then re-plan as dependencies appear
options.d: Pick the largest files first and write tests for them until time runs out

explanation.c: An open-ended task is mapped first and planned from what is found.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a fixed order cannot follow the findings: "a pipeline that marches through steps that no longer make sense".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a plan made before any ground truth is a guess: "the plan is made before any ground truth exists".
explanation.d: Ruled out because size is not impact: "mapped, ranked and then planned again as dependencies appear".

quizzes.stem: In an adaptive investigation the step chooser keeps proposing "list the test files", which was already done, and the loop hits its step limit each time. What is the best change?

options.a: Double the step limit so that the planner has room to move on by itself
options.b: Halt with a stuck status once a task repeats, and name the repeated one
options.c: Remove the planner's history so that every request is judged on its own
options.d: Let the worker skip the repeated subtask silently and carry on with the next

explanation.b: A repeated subtask is a lack of progress, and a status says so.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the limit is a backstop and the cause is the lack of progress: "A loop that runs into it needs a progress check".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the history is what lets the planner see what it has done: "The planner is given the goal and the steps done so far".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a silent skip leaves no status behind: "so that a reader of the result can tell them apart".

quizzes.stem: A large review runs one pass per module and then a final pass across modules. What should the final pass receive?

options.a: The full text of every module, so that it can read the code that it compares
options.b: The findings of the earlier passes together with the diff of the whole change
options.c: The diff of the whole change, because the modules are in the repository already
options.d: A name and a short summary for each, listing what it offers and what it expects

explanation.d: Summaries are the interface between the passes.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the text would bring the overload back: "the one overloaded request that the split removed".
explanation.b: Ruled out because findings alone say nothing about what the files offer: "what the file offers (the functions and types others use, with their parameters)".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the final pass needs each file's conclusions: "The cross pass needs what each file pass concluded about what the file offers".

quizzes.stem: A platform team runs one fixed checklist (lint, test, report) over forty unrelated systems. A colleague wants an adaptive planner for each because it is more capable. What is the best answer?

options.a: Use it, because a planner improves on a fixed checklist of steps in every respect
options.b: Use one planner for the forty of them in a single shared session instead
options.c: Use the plain sequence on each, as the steps are known and none affects another
options.d: Use a pass for each plus a cross pass, because that many items need a cross pass

explanation.c: Known steps and independent items call for the simplest shape.
explanation.a: Ruled out because capability has a price: "Agentic systems often trade latency and cost for better task performance."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the systems do not interact, so nothing is gained by a shared planner: "A fixed chain, run once for each item".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a cross pass is for items that affect each other: "Items that do not (forty services, each given the same checklist) need only the chain, run forty times."

quizzes.stem: A team's adaptive investigation asks the planner for each next step, but shows it only its own earlier plan text and not what the earlier work produced. After a few steps the plan drifts away from the true state of the code. What fixes it?

options.a: Ask it to restate the goal more carefully before each next step
options.b: Plan every step up front, so that no drift is possible
options.c: Hand it the output of each action so far, such as a test run or a file listing
options.d: Switch to a fixed chain, since a chain cannot drift from the code

explanation.c: The planner needs ground truth from each step, not its own earlier guesses.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the source of the drift is what it is shown: "a plan that is made from the model's own previous guesses drifts".
explanation.b: Ruled out because an up-front plan has no results to use: "the plan is made before any ground truth exists".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a chain does not adapt: "If step two finds that step three is pointless, the chain runs step three."

quizzes.stem: A source file has four thousand lines, which is too long for one pass. How should it be handled?

options.a: Send its first part only, because the beginning of a file is the most important
options.b: Summarise the file in one sentence and use the sentence in its place
options.c: Send the whole file anyway, because splitting loses what connects its separate parts
options.d: Inspect it in labelled parts, and let the joined summaries carry what spans them

explanation.d: Parts keep each pass small and the summary joins them.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the rest of the file would never be reviewed: "A file that does not fit a pass of its own is cut into parts of a fixed number of lines".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a sentence does not carry the interfaces: "what the file offers (the functions and types others use, with their parameters)".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the whole file brings back the problem of the split: "spends that budget on text before the review begins".
